notes:
Summary: Auric Lockbox builds sensitive-document classification and automated redaction for regulated finance clients. Primary requirement: private VPC deployment with customer-managed keys (BYOK) and HSM-level protection. They will only accept HSM-backed keys (FIPS 140-2 Level 3/4 preference) and require integration options across AWS KMS (import key material), Azure Key Vault Managed HSM, and GCP External KMS. Key details and asks:
- Envelope encryption mandatory; platform should never persist plaintext keys.
- Support for AWS KMS CMKs with imported key material (IKM) and key policies that prevent Redwood from exporting key material.
- Azure: require Managed HSM with RBAC mappings and soft-delete/ purge retention settings documented.
- GCP: External Key Manager (EKM) compatibility and CMEK-style integrations.
- BYOK HSM options: compatibility with Thales Luna and YubiHSM for on-prem key custody.
- Key rotation cadence: quarterly minimum, automated rotation tooling + versioning audit trail.
- Audit logging: full KMS operation logs forwarded to their Splunk SIEM; retention 7 years for audit events related to keys and model access.
- Data residency: inference logs and model artifacts must be stored in US and EU regions only; control plane allowed in NA.
- Compliance: SOC2 Type II report required; legal also prefers ISO27001.
- Performance: acceptable token latency impact <= +10ms median for envelope crypto operations; need benchmark with Dedicated deployment on NVidia A800.
Quoted from security lead: "We cannot accept any key exfiltration risk. Keys must be under our control and auditable end-to-end."
